wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value: State-backed housing agency offering repayment help and program info.
Visit PHFA
https://www.phfa.org/
This resource is designed for homeowners in early-stage financial distress:
Homeowners 1–2 Months Behind: Individuals who have missed a payment or two and believe they can catch up with the right guidance and support programs.
First-Time Borrowers Unsure of Options: People who don't know what resources exist at the state level for mortgage relief, refinancing, or forbearance.
Those Wanting to Act Before Foreclosure: Homeowners who want to take proactive steps now, before their situation escalates to legal proceedings.

The Pennsylvania Housing Finance Agency (PHFA) is a state-backed organization that connects homeowners with repayment assistance programs, refinancing options, and forbearance plans.
Program Review: PHFA reviews your current mortgage situation and identifies which state-level programs you may qualify for, including loan modifications and temporary payment relief.
Counselor Connection: They can connect you directly with HUD-approved housing counselors in your area who specialize in negotiating with lenders on your behalf.
Application Guidance: PHFA walks you through the application process for programs like HEMAP, ensuring your paperwork is complete and submitted correctly.
Ongoing Support: Even after enrollment, PHFA provides follow-up resources to help you stay on track with your mortgage payments and avoid future distress.
Take the First Step Toward Stability
PHFA can review your options — including refinancing and forbearance — before foreclosure starts. There is no cost to explore what's available to you.
Free legal help for foreclosure defense and consumer rights.
Find Legal Help
https://palegalaid.net/find-legal-help
This resource is designed for homeowners facing legal action:
Homeowners Who Received a Court Letter: Individuals who have been served with a foreclosure notice or summons and need to understand their legal rights.
Those Who Can't Afford an Attorney: Low-to-moderate income homeowners who need professional legal representation but cannot pay for private counsel.
People Unsure How to Respond: Homeowners who received legal paperwork and don't know what steps to take or what deadlines they're facing.

The Pennsylvania Legal Aid Network (PLAN) provides free legal assistance to homeowners dealing with foreclosure proceedings and consumer rights issues.
Case Review: A legal aid attorney reviews your foreclosure documents, court filings, and mortgage history to identify potential defenses or violations by the lender.
Court Representation: In qualifying cases, PLAN can represent you in court, file responses on your behalf, and negotiate directly with the lender's legal team.
Rights Education: PLAN explains your rights under Pennsylvania foreclosure law, including mandatory mediation requirements and notice periods that lenders must follow.
Referral Network: If your case requires specialized assistance beyond PLAN's scope, they connect you with other legal organizations and housing resources in your area.
Protect Your Rights — Get Free Legal Help
PLAN can review your paperwork and explain your legal rights at no cost. Don't face foreclosure proceedings alone.
Certified advisors who help negotiate with lenders.
Find a Counselor
https://www.hud.gov/program_offices/housing/sfh/hcc
This resource is designed for homeowners who need help communicating with their lender:
Homeowners in Early-Stage Distress: Individuals who have fallen behind on payments and need someone experienced to help negotiate a solution with their mortgage company.
Those Intimidated by the Process: People who feel overwhelmed by lender phone calls, paperwork, and confusing modification applications.
Borrowers Seeking Loan Modifications: Homeowners who want to explore options like interest rate reductions, term extensions, or partial claim agreements.

HUD-Approved Housing Counselors are certified professionals trained to help homeowners navigate mortgage distress and communicate effectively with lenders.
Lender Negotiation: A HUD counselor can join your calls with the lender, present your financial situation clearly, and advocate for modification options you may not know about.
Budget Analysis: Counselors review your full financial picture — income, expenses, debts — to build a realistic repayment proposal that lenders are more likely to accept.
Program Matching: They identify federal, state, and local assistance programs you qualify for and help you apply, ensuring nothing falls through the cracks.
Free and Confidential: All HUD-approved counseling services are provided at no cost to you. Your financial information is kept strictly confidential.
Get Expert Help With Your Lender
A HUD counselor can help you call your lender and explore modification programs — completely free of charge.
Nonprofit credit and housing support.
Visit Clarifi
https://clarifi.org
This resource is designed for families needing financial stabilization:
Families Needing Budget Help: Households where monthly expenses have exceeded income, making it difficult to keep up with mortgage payments alongside other bills.
Homeowners Seeking Mortgage Relief Guidance: Individuals who know help exists but need a trusted nonprofit to walk them through the options step by step.
Those Wanting Long-Term Financial Health: People who want more than a quick fix — they want to build a sustainable budget and avoid future financial crises.

NeighborWorks / Clarifi is a nonprofit organization serving Pennsylvania and New Jersey that provides comprehensive credit counseling and housing support services.
Budget Stabilization: Clarifi counselors work with you to create a realistic monthly budget that prioritizes your mortgage while addressing other essential expenses.
Mortgage Relief Navigation: They guide you through available relief programs, help you prepare applications, and follow up with servicers to ensure your case progresses.
Credit Counseling: Beyond immediate mortgage help, Clarifi offers credit counseling to help you understand your credit report, dispute errors, and build a path toward financial recovery.
Community Resources: As part of the NeighborWorks network, Clarifi connects you with additional community resources including utility assistance, food programs, and employment services.
Start Stabilizing Your Finances Today
Clarifi helps families stabilize budgets and manage mortgage relief programs. All services are provided by trained nonprofit counselors.
Foreclosure and consumer defense legal aid.
Get Legal Aid
https://nlsa.us/
This resource is designed for Western PA homeowners in legal jeopardy:
Western PA Homeowners Facing Foreclosure: Individuals in the western part of the state who have received foreclosure notices and need immediate legal guidance.
Those Dealing with Predatory Lending: Homeowners who suspect they were victims of unfair lending practices, deceptive terms, or illegal fees.
People Needing Help Responding to Court Filings: Anyone who has received legal documents related to their property and doesn't know how to respond within required timelines.

Neighborhood Legal Services (NLS) provides free legal assistance to low-income residents of Western Pennsylvania facing foreclosure and consumer protection issues.
Foreclosure Defense: NLS attorneys review your case, identify potential defenses, and represent you in court proceedings to protect your home and your rights.
Consumer Protection: If your lender has engaged in predatory practices — such as hidden fees, misleading terms, or improper notice — NLS can pursue legal remedies on your behalf.
Document Review: NLS reviews all foreclosure-related documents, including the original mortgage, modification denials, and court filings, to find errors or violations.
Community Outreach: NLS holds regular clinics and workshops in Western PA communities, making it easier to access legal help close to home.
Know Your Rights — Get Free Legal Help
NLS can walk you through your rights and help you respond to foreclosure notices at no cost.
Civil legal help for Bucks, Montgomery, Chester, and Delaware Counties.
Contact LASP
https://lasp.org
This resource is designed for Southeastern PA homeowners needing legal support:
Bucks, Montgomery, Chester, and Delaware County Residents: Homeowners in these four counties who are facing foreclosure or housing-related legal issues.
Those Needing Free Legal Representation: Low-income individuals who qualify for free legal counsel and may need an attorney to represent them in court.
Homeowners Facing Eviction After Foreclosure: People who have lost their home to foreclosure and need help understanding their remaining rights and timelines.

Legal Aid of Southeastern PA (LASP) provides free civil legal assistance to residents of Bucks, Montgomery, Chester, and Delaware Counties in Pennsylvania.
Free Legal Advice: LASP attorneys provide confidential consultations to help you understand your legal situation, your rights, and your options moving forward.
Court Representation: In qualifying cases, LASP will represent you in court — filing motions, attending hearings, and negotiating with opposing counsel on your behalf.
Foreclosure Mediation Support: LASP can accompany you through Pennsylvania's mandatory foreclosure mediation process, ensuring your interests are properly represented.
Housing Rights Advocacy: Beyond foreclosure, LASP handles cases involving landlord-tenant disputes, housing discrimination, and other civil legal matters affecting your home.
Get Free Legal Advice in Your County
LASP offers free legal advice and may even represent you in court if needed. Services cover Bucks, Montgomery, Chester, and Delaware Counties.
State loan program to catch up on mortgage payments (up to $60K / 24 months).
Learn About HEMAP
https://phfa.org/counseling/hemap.aspx
This resource is designed for homeowners with temporary financial hardship:
Homeowners Who Lost Income Temporarily: Individuals who experienced a job loss, medical emergency, or other hardship that caused them to fall behind on mortgage payments.
Those Who Can Resume Payments Soon: Borrowers whose financial situation is stabilizing and who can resume regular mortgage payments once their arrears are caught up.
People Needing Help Paying Back Mortgage Arrears: Homeowners who owe several months of back payments and need direct financial assistance to bring their mortgage current.

The Homeowners Emergency Mortgage Assistance Program (HEMAP) is a Pennsylvania state loan program that helps homeowners catch up on delinquent mortgage payments — providing up to $60,000 over 24 months.
Direct Arrears Payment: HEMAP pays your past-due mortgage payments directly to your lender, bringing your account current so you can avoid foreclosure.
State-Backed Loan: The assistance is structured as a no-interest loan from the state. Repayment terms are manageable and designed around your financial recovery.
Counselor-Assisted Application: You apply through a HUD-approved housing counselor who helps you gather documentation, complete forms, and submit everything correctly.
Eligibility Review: HEMAP evaluates your situation to confirm that your hardship is temporary and that you have a reasonable ability to resume payments. This protects both you and the program.
Apply Through a Housing Counselor
HEMAP can step in to help pay arrears directly to your lender. Apply through a counselor to get started.
COVID-related grant (up to $30K) for mortgage, taxes, or utilities.
Apply at PAHAF
https://pahaf.org/
This resource is designed for homeowners needing one-time financial relief:
COVID-Impacted Homeowners: Individuals whose income was reduced or disrupted due to the pandemic and who are still catching up on housing-related expenses.
Those Behind on Property Taxes or Utilities: Homeowners who owe back taxes, water/sewer bills, or utility payments that threaten their housing stability.
People Seeking Grant Assistance (Not a Loan): Homeowners who need financial help but want relief that does not need to be repaid.

The PA Homeowner Assistance Fund (PAHAF) provides grants of up to $30,000 to eligible Pennsylvania homeowners for mortgage payments, property taxes, and utility costs.
Grant — Not a Loan: Unlike many assistance programs, PAHAF provides grant funding. If approved, the money does not need to be repaid.
Broad Coverage: Funds can be applied to past-due mortgage payments, delinquent property taxes, water and sewer bills, and other housing-related costs that jeopardize your home.
Online Application: The application process is handled online through the PAHAF portal. You'll need to provide income documentation, proof of hardship, and details about your delinquent accounts.
Direct Payment to Servicers: Approved funds are sent directly to your mortgage servicer, tax authority, or utility company — ensuring the money goes exactly where it's needed.
See If You Qualify for Grant Relief
PAHAF can provide a one-time grant to help you stabilize housing costs. Funds do not need to be repaid.
Emergency assistance for utilities, rent, mortgage, and essential bills.
Call 211
https://uwp.org/211
This resource is designed for anyone needing immediate relief for basic expenses:
Homeowners Behind on Essential Bills: Individuals who can't cover utilities, rent, or mortgage this month and need emergency funding to stay afloat.
Families in Crisis: Households dealing with sudden income loss, medical emergencies, or other crises that have disrupted their ability to pay for basic needs.
People Who Don't Know Where to Start: Anyone feeling overwhelmed by their situation who needs a single point of contact to find local funding and support programs.

Catholic Social Services and United Way 211 provide emergency assistance and connect individuals with local funding sources for utilities, rent, mortgage, and other essential expenses.
211 Helpline: By dialing 2-1-1, you're connected to a trained specialist who assesses your needs and matches you with local programs that can help — from utility shutoff prevention to emergency rent assistance.
Emergency Funding: Catholic Social Services and partner agencies offer direct financial assistance for qualifying households, covering immediate needs like past-due utility bills and mortgage payments.
Comprehensive Referrals: Beyond financial help, 211 connects you with food banks, healthcare services, mental health support, and other community resources.
No Wrong Door: You don't need to know the right program name or agency. 211 serves as a single entry point that routes you to the help you need based on your situation.
Get Connected to Emergency Help
If you need quick relief for essential bills, start with 211 for local funding sources. Help is available now.

item.title: PA Law Help: A Guide to Bankruptcy
item.dc:creator: info@tbonejones.com

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value: Educational guide on Chapter 7 and Chapter 13 bankruptcy options.
Read the Guide
https://www.palawhelp.org/resource/a-guide-to-bankruptcy
This resource is designed for homeowners exploring bankruptcy as an option:
Homeowners Considering Bankruptcy: Individuals who are overwhelmed by debt and want to understand whether Chapter 7 or Chapter 13 might provide relief.
Those Who Want to Understand the Process: People who have heard about bankruptcy but don't know what it involves, what it protects, or how it affects their home.
Anyone Wanting to Make an Informed Decision: Homeowners who want to weigh all options — including bankruptcy — before committing to a path forward.

PA Law Help's Guide to Bankruptcy is a free educational resource that explains Chapter 7 and Chapter 13 bankruptcy options in plain language for Pennsylvania residents.
Chapter 7 vs. Chapter 13: The guide breaks down the key differences — Chapter 7 liquidates certain assets to discharge debts, while Chapter 13 creates a repayment plan that can help you keep your home.
Homestead Protections: Learn how Pennsylvania's exemption laws protect certain property and equity during bankruptcy proceedings, so you understand what's at risk and what's protected.
The Filing Process: Step-by-step explanation of what happens when you file, from the automatic stay that halts foreclosure to the discharge of qualifying debts.
When to Seek Legal Help: The guide helps you identify when it's time to consult with a bankruptcy attorney and how to find free legal assistance if you can't afford one.
Learn How Bankruptcy Could Help
This guide helps you understand how bankruptcy might reset your financial situation. Knowledge is the first step.
Nonprofit debt management counseling.
Contact CCCS
https://www.cccspa.org/
This resource is designed for homeowners dealing with overwhelming debt:
Homeowners Drowning in Debt: Individuals whose total debt obligations have become unmanageable, making it impossible to keep up with mortgage payments.
Those Wanting to Negotiate Before Legal Action: People who want to work out a debt management plan with creditors before the situation escalates to court.
Anyone Seeking Professional Budget Guidance: Homeowners who need expert help creating a realistic repayment strategy that prioritizes keeping their home.

The Consumer Credit Counseling Service (CCCS) is a nonprofit organization that provides professional debt management counseling to help homeowners regain control of their finances.
Debt Management Plans: CCCS negotiates directly with your creditors to reduce interest rates, waive fees, and create a single consolidated monthly payment you can afford.
Budget Counseling: Certified counselors analyze your income, expenses, and debts to build a personalized budget that prioritizes your mortgage and essential bills.
Creditor Communication: CCCS handles communication with creditors on your behalf, reducing the stress of collection calls and helping you avoid further legal action.
Long-Term Financial Education: Beyond immediate debt relief, CCCS provides workshops and resources to help you build lasting financial habits and avoid future crises.
Start Managing Your Debt Today
CCCS helps homeowners negotiate debt plans before legal action starts. All counseling is confidential and nonprofit.
Free consultations for low-income residents.
Find a Clinic
https://palegalaid.net/find-legal-help
This resource is designed for low-income homeowners weighing bankruptcy:
Low-Income Homeowners: Individuals who meet income eligibility guidelines and need professional bankruptcy advice they cannot afford on their own.
Those Unsure If Bankruptcy Is Right: People who want to sit down with an attorney to discuss whether filing makes sense for their specific situation.
Homeowners Needing Help With Paperwork: Individuals who have decided to file but need assistance completing the complex bankruptcy petition and schedules.

Legal Aid Bankruptcy Clinics offer free one-on-one consultations with attorneys who specialize in bankruptcy law, specifically serving low-income Pennsylvania residents.
Free Attorney Consultation: You'll meet with a qualified bankruptcy attorney who reviews your financial situation and explains whether Chapter 7 or Chapter 13 is appropriate for your case.
Eligibility Screening: Clinic staff help determine if you meet income and asset thresholds for bankruptcy filing, and which chapter provides the best outcome for your home.
Filing Assistance: For those who decide to proceed, clinic attorneys can help prepare and file the necessary paperwork, including schedules, means tests, and creditor matrices.
Ongoing Support: Many clinics provide follow-up appointments to help you navigate the bankruptcy process from filing through discharge, including attending the 341 meeting of creditors.
Schedule a Free Bankruptcy Consultation
You can meet with a legal aid attorney to discuss whether bankruptcy fits your case — completely free.

item.title: County Register of Wills / Estate Services
item.dc:creator: info@tbonejones.com

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value: Handles probate or estate transfer of title.
Visit Register of Wills
https://buckscounty.gov/166/Register-of-Wills
This resource is designed for heirs and beneficiaries of inherited property:
Heirs of an Inherited Home: Individuals who have inherited a property and need to transfer the title into their name through the probate process.
Family Members Handling an Estate: People responsible for settling a deceased family member's estate, including real property and outstanding debts.
Those Wanting to Sell an Inherited Property: Heirs who want to sell the property but first need to establish clear legal ownership through probate court.

The County Register of Wills handles probate proceedings and estate transfers, helping heirs establish legal ownership of inherited property.
Probate Filing: The Register of Wills guides you through filing the necessary probate documents to legally transfer property title from a deceased owner to their heirs.
Estate Administration: For estates with a will, the office helps appoint an executor and oversee the distribution of assets according to the deceased's wishes.
Intestacy Process: If there is no will, the Register of Wills handles the intestacy process, determining who inherits the property under Pennsylvania law.
Title Clearance: Once probate is complete, the office issues the documentation needed to clear title on the property, allowing you to sell, refinance, or manage it freely.
Start the Probate Process
They can guide you through transferring or selling an inherited home legally. Start with your county's Register of Wills.
Handles vacant property issues and lien relief.
Contact Planning Commission
https://buckscounty.gov/272/Planning-Commission
This resource is designed for owners of vacant or distressed properties:
Owners Facing Blight Violations: Individuals who have received code enforcement notices for property maintenance issues, overgrown lots, or structural problems.
Those Wanting to Sell Vacant Property As-Is: Homeowners who want to dispose of a vacant or distressed property without investing in costly repairs.
People Dealing with Municipal Liens: Property owners with accumulated liens from unpaid fines, utilities, or taxes who need help resolving them before a sale.

Local Code Enforcement and Land Bank programs help property owners address vacant property issues, resolve blight violations, and navigate lien relief options.
Code Violation Resolution: Code enforcement can work with you to create a compliance plan for addressing property violations, often with reasonable timelines rather than immediate penalties.
Land Bank Programs: Some municipalities operate land banks that can acquire distressed properties, clear liens, and return them to productive use — providing owners with a clean exit.
Lien Negotiation: In many cases, accumulated municipal liens can be negotiated down or structured into payment plans, making it feasible to sell or transfer the property.
As-Is Sale Options: If the property is beyond repair, code enforcement and the land bank can guide you through options for selling the property in its current condition.
Address Your Property Issues
The land bank can help if you're facing blight violations or want to sell as-is. Start by contacting your local planning commission.
Internal referral to Offer to Buy, Subject-To, or Sell-For-You team.
Sell Now
https://wayoutnow.com/sell-now
This resource is designed for homeowners ready to explore selling options:
Homeowners Who'd Rather Not Handle Repairs Alone: Individuals who don't have the time, money, or energy to fix up a property before selling it on the open market.
Those Navigating Probate or Complex Title Issues: People dealing with inherited properties, liens, or title complications who need an experienced team to handle the details.
Anyone Ready for a Fresh Start: Homeowners who have decided that selling — quickly and with minimal hassle — is the best path forward for their situation.

Way Out Now Partner Path is our internal referral program that connects homeowners with our team for direct purchase offers, subject-to arrangements, or full-service sell-for-you solutions.
Direct Offer to Buy: We evaluate your property and present a fair cash offer, allowing you to sell quickly without listing, showings, or real estate commissions.
Subject-To Solutions: In some cases, we can take over your existing mortgage payments through a subject-to arrangement, relieving you of the financial burden while protecting your credit.
Sell-For-You Service: If your property has market value that would benefit from a traditional sale, our team handles everything — repairs, listing, showings, and closing — on your behalf.
Personalized Consultation: Every situation is different. We start with a no-pressure consultation to understand your goals and recommend the option that best fits your needs.
Explore Your Selling Options
If you'd rather not handle repairs or probate alone, we can help you transition smoothly. Start with a free consultation.

item.title: County Family Services (e.g., Bucks County MH/DS)
item.dc:creator: info@tbonejones.com

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value: Counseling and mediation for family transitions.
Visit Bucks County Services
https://buckscounty.gov/
This resource is designed for homeowners navigating personal and family challenges:
Homeowners Going Through Divorce: Individuals whose marriage is ending and who need support navigating the emotional and financial impact on their housing situation.
Those Dealing with Loss or Grief: People who have lost a family member and are struggling with both the emotional weight and the practical decisions around the family home.
Families in Transition: Households experiencing major life changes — relocation, caregiving responsibilities, or blended family dynamics — that affect their housing stability.

County Family Services provides counseling, mediation, and support resources for individuals and families navigating difficult personal transitions that affect their housing situation.
Individual Counseling: Licensed counselors provide confidential sessions to help you process grief, stress, anxiety, and other emotions that can accompany housing instability.
Family Mediation: When family disagreements complicate housing decisions — such as what to do with a shared or inherited property — trained mediators help facilitate productive conversations.
Crisis Intervention: For families in acute crisis, county services can connect you with emergency mental health support, temporary housing, and safety planning resources.
Referral Coordination: Family Services works with housing counselors, legal aid, and financial assistance programs to ensure you're getting comprehensive support — not just emotional care.
Get Support for Your Family's Transition
Family Services can connect you with counselors and resources for stability during difficult times.
Statewide human services directory.
Call 211
https://uwp.org/211
This resource is designed for anyone managing more than just a financial crisis:
People Managing Emotional and Financial Stress: Individuals whose housing problems are compounded by anxiety, depression, or emotional exhaustion.
Those Needing Family or Relationship Help: People dealing with family conflict, domestic issues, or relationship strain alongside their housing situation.
Anyone Unsure Where to Turn: Individuals who feel lost in the system and need a single phone call to connect with the right combination of services.

United Way 211 is a free, confidential helpline that connects individuals and families with local human services — from mental health support to housing assistance.
24/7 Helpline: Dial 2-1-1 any time, day or night, to speak with a trained specialist who can assess your needs and connect you with appropriate local services.
Comprehensive Service Directory: 211 maintains a database of thousands of local programs covering mental health, substance abuse, domestic violence, food assistance, housing, and more.
Personalized Referrals: Specialists don't just read from a list — they listen to your situation and make targeted referrals to programs that match your specific needs and location.
Follow-Up Support: Many 211 centers offer follow-up calls to make sure you were able to connect with the referred services and to provide additional referrals if needed.
Connect With Help Beyond Housing
If you're managing more than just finances, 211 can link you to emotional, family, and practical support.

item.title: Way Out Now Rent-Back / Lease Transition
item.dc:creator: info@tbonejones.com

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value: Internal partner solution for homeowners needing time to move.
Schedule a Consultation
https://wayoutnow.com/consultation
This resource is designed for homeowners who need to sell but aren't ready to move:
Homeowners Needing Time to Relocate: Individuals who want to sell their property but need additional weeks or months to find new housing and coordinate their move.
Families with School-Age Children: Parents who want to sell but need to time the transition around the school year to minimize disruption for their kids.
Those Seeking Financial Relief Without Displacement: Homeowners who want the financial burden of ownership lifted but need the stability of staying in their home temporarily.

Way Out Now's Rent-Back / Lease Transition program allows homeowners to sell their property and remain in the home as a renter during their transition period.
Sell and Stay: After closing, you can continue living in the home under a short-term lease agreement, giving you time to plan your next move without the pressure of an immediate vacancy.
Flexible Terms: Lease-back periods are negotiated based on your needs — whether you need 30 days, 90 days, or longer to find your next home.
Reduced Financial Pressure: By selling, you eliminate mortgage payments, property taxes, insurance, and maintenance costs. Your rent-back payment is typically lower than your previous total housing expense.
Smooth Transition Support: Our team helps coordinate the transition, connecting you with moving resources, new housing options, and any other support you need during the process.
Sell Your Home and Stay While You Transition
We can help you sell and stay temporarily to create a smooth transition. Schedule a free consultation to learn more.
Assistance for FHA-backed mortgages.
Learn About FHA Options
https://www.hud.gov/program_offices/housing/sfh/nsc/lossmit
This resource is designed for homeowners with FHA-insured mortgages:
FHA Borrowers Facing Hardship: Individuals with Federal Housing Administration-backed mortgages who have experienced income loss, medical expenses, or other financial setbacks.
Those Behind on FHA Loan Payments: Homeowners who have missed payments on their FHA mortgage and want to explore alternatives to foreclosure.
People Unaware of FHA-Specific Programs: Borrowers who don't realize that FHA loans come with built-in loss mitigation options that conventional loans may not offer.

The FHA Loss Mitigation Program provides specialized assistance options for homeowners with FHA-insured mortgages who are struggling to make their payments.
Special Forbearance: FHA may approve a temporary reduction or suspension of your mortgage payments while you recover from a financial hardship, with a structured plan to catch up afterward.
Loan Modification: Your lender can modify your FHA loan terms — extending the repayment period, reducing the interest rate, or adding missed payments to the loan balance — to create a more affordable monthly payment.
Partial Claim: FHA's partial claim option allows HUD to provide a one-time payment to your lender to bring your mortgage current. This creates a second, interest-free lien that isn't due until you sell or refinance.
Pre-Foreclosure Sale: If keeping the home isn't viable, FHA allows a pre-foreclosure sale (similar to a short sale) that lets you sell the property for less than the mortgage balance without owing the difference.
Explore Your FHA Relief Options
FHA may allow repayment plans or modifications before foreclosure. Contact your servicer or a HUD counselor to get started.
Help for USDA or RHS loans in rural PA.
Visit USDA Rural Development
https://www.rd.usda.gov/
This resource is designed for rural Pennsylvania homeowners with USDA loans:
Rural PA Homeowners with USDA/RHS Loans: Individuals in rural areas who financed their home through the USDA Rural Housing Service and are now facing financial difficulty.
Borrowers Experiencing Agricultural or Seasonal Income Loss: Homeowners whose income fluctuates with farming seasons or rural employment cycles and who have fallen behind.
Those Unaware of USDA-Specific Hardship Options: Borrowers who don't know that USDA loans include unique loss mitigation programs tailored to rural communities.

The Rural Housing Service (USDA) provides specialized assistance for homeowners in rural Pennsylvania who have USDA-backed mortgages and are experiencing financial hardship.
Payment Moratorium: USDA can approve a temporary suspension of mortgage payments for borrowers facing circumstances beyond their control, such as job loss or natural disaster.
Loan Reamortization: Your USDA loan can be reamortized to extend the repayment term, reducing your monthly payment to a more affordable level based on your current income.
Interest Rate Reduction: In some cases, USDA can reduce the interest rate on your loan to lower your payment, particularly if market rates have dropped since your original financing.
Protective Advances: USDA may make protective advance payments for property taxes or insurance on your behalf to prevent tax sales or lapsed coverage while you recover financially.
Check Your USDA Loan Options
If your loan is rural-based, USDA can review special hardship options designed specifically for rural communities.
